newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: UAE bunkers to keep price advantage - consultant.
newsitem.headline: UAE bunkers to keep price advantage - consultant.

text.p: Oil bunker export prices in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) will stay cheaper than rival ship fuelling centres in Singapore, Europe and the U.S. Gulf coast, an oil consultant said on Wednesday.

UAE bunker fuel oil prices would average $84 a tonne in the year 2000, compared to $92 in Singapore and $90 in the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp (ARA) region, according to a paper presented by Robin Meech, senior manager at Arthur D Little International, at an energy conference in Abu Dhabi.
A $1 price advantage for UAE bunkers compared to prices in the U.S. Gulf coast market moved out to a $12 dollar premium in the year 2000 and then $17 in 2005.
UAE bunkers averaged a $4 a tonne discount in 1996 to Singapore's average bunker prices of $108, Meech's paper showed.
Bunker prices in the UAE port of Fujairah are frequently cheaper because of the region's large simple distillation refining capacity and lower operating and supply costs at Gulf bunker terminals.
Shippers use Fujairah to refuel before loading crude tankers with oil from Gulf producers.
Middle East bunker supplies would grow seven percent a year over the next seven to eight years because of growing crude production from the region and refinery expansions, Meech said.
"The Middle East will be the fastest growing supply region," he told conference delegates.
